title: List.Perm is symmetric
statement: For any two lists l1, l2 over Nat, if List.Perm l1 l2 computes to true then List.Perm l2 l1 also computes to true.

formal.statement: theorem List.perm_symm : ((x0 : List.{0} AxNat) -> ((x1 : List.{0} AxNat) -> ((x2 : Eq.{1} Bool (List.Perm x0 x1) Bool.true) -> Eq.{1} Bool (List.Perm x1 x0) Bool.true)))

evidence.supports: List.perm_symm is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example list_theorem_inventory -- List.perm_symm 2>/dev/null | grep -Fc '((x0 : List.{0} AxNat) -> ((x1 : List.{0} AxNat) -> ((x2 : Eq.{1} Bool (List.Perm x0 x1) Bool.true) -> Eq.{1} Bool (List.Perm x1 x0) Bool.true)))')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pattern is the FULL admitted type (rendered by Kernel::render_lean via list_theorem_inventory), not the theorem's name -- a drifted statement would fail this check.

evidence.supports: The List/Nat operations this statement is about COMPUTE the intended values, with negative controls -- the kernel cannot tell a Definition is wrong.
evidence.notes: The list_prelude:: sweep (list_prelude_tests.rs, bridge_tests.rs, perm_tests.rs) reduces List/Nat.Multiset operations to concrete numerals or nil/cons skeletons at tiny discriminating arguments and pairs positives with negative controls.

provenance.source: theorem name and canonical type read directly via list_theorem_inventory, which prints render_lean of the admitted type; declared by list_prelude/perm.rs (lane list-carrier-2, ADR-1583 amending ADR-1579).

notes: The one theorem of the four that needs to relate the two lists' bounds: the hypothesis (via Nat.Finset.allBelow_true_at) only gives the pointwise count-agreement fact below bound(l1,l2), and the goal needs it below bound(l2,l1) -- two different terms (succ (add (max l1) (max l2)) vs succ (add (max l2) (max l1))). Closed with Nat.add_comm plus a succ congruence proving Eq (bound l1 l2) (bound l2 l1) outright, then ops::transport_along (a new small generalization of the Eq.rec-based combinators already in list_prelude/ops.rs) to move the bound-membership hypothesis across it.
